proof:
# The sharp inverse-energy cap certificate is not preserved by anchored mixing

Write V=|K|, E=E_K(y), Gamma=(d/(d+1))^d, and

    F_d(alpha)=((d+1)^(d+1)/d^d) alpha(1-alpha^(1/d)),
    D_K(y)=V F_d^(-1)(E/V).

The sharp containing-cap theorem proves that D is a lower bound on the
actual ordinary raw depth. This note tests that particular certificate,
not the actual depth, energy concavity, or OC.

## 1. Exact failure under inclusion in every d>=2

Let T be any d-simplex, of volume V, let y=g_T, and choose one apex P
opposite its facet F. Write c=g_F. For s>1 put

    P_s=c+s(P-c),       T_s=conv(F,P_s).

Then T is contained in T_s and |T_s|=sV. The barycentric coordinates of
the fixed mark y in T_s are

    beta_apex=1/((d+1)s),
    beta_j=((d+1)s-1)/(d(d+1)s),  j on the base.

For any simplex S and interior barycentric mark beta, the exact energy
is |S|(d+1)^(d+1) product beta_j. One can verify this independently:
if positive affine denominator values at the vertices are l_j, their
constraint is sum beta_j l_j=1, and the projective integral is
|S|/product l_j. Weighted AM--GM gives the unique optimum
l_j=1/((d+1)beta_j). Consequently

    E_(T_s)(y)=V[((d+1)-1/s)/d]^d > V=E_T(y).          (1)

Nevertheless,

    D_(T_s)(y) < Gamma V = D_T(y),  for EVERY s>1.     (2)

To prove this set q=s^(-1/d) in (0,1) and

    G(q)=((d+1-q^d)/d)^d.

With A=(d+1-q^d)/d, direct differentiation gives

    G''(q)=(d-1)(d+1)q^(d-2) A^(d-2)(q^d-1)<0.

Since G(1)=1 and G'(1)=-d, strict concavity yields

    G(q)<d+1-dq.

Dividing by s and using (1), this says exactly

    E_(T_s)(y)/|T_s| < F_d(Gamma/s).

The strict increase of F_d on [0,Gamma] proves (2). This proof also
shows why d=1 is different: G is affine and D is the actual interval
depth. For reference, as s tends to infinity,

    D_(T_s)(y) -> V/(d+1),

because F_d(alpha)/alpha tends to (d+1)^(d+1)/d^d at zero.

A fully rational planar calibration is s=4. In that case

    E_(T_4)(y)/|T_4|=121/256 < 1/2=F_2(1/9),

so D_(T_4)(y)<4V/9 although T is contained in T_4. No numerical
evaluation of an inverse function is involved.

## 2. An actual three-fiber failure of the proposed superlevel rule

Take the lifted convex hull with fibers T at bases -1 and 1, and T_s at
base 0. Its projection is [-1,1] and its integer fibers are EXACTLY
T,T_s,T: every endpoint interpolation at zero is T, already in T_s.
All marks are the same point y. Thus the integer-anchored relation

    (0,y)=((-1,y)+(1,y))/2

is actual, and the target contains the endpoint Minkowski average.
Joint energy-root concavity is respected, indeed strictly by (1).
But (2) gives

    D_(T_s)(y)^(1/d)
      < [D_T(y)^(1/d)+D_T(y)^(1/d)]/2.

Therefore inverse-energy certified cap mass, its dth root, and its
fiberwise superlevel sets do NOT give the proposed anchored concavity.
This is not a failure of true ordinary depth: inclusion makes true
unnormalized depth nondecreasing.

## 3. Opposite numeric offsets alone give only one source credit

There is also a sharp bounded warning for endpoint cap sums. For any
d>=2 take a centered simplex T of volume V and a direction x_1 in which
its vertex cap at zero has fraction Gamma. Normalize its heights to
[-1,d]. Let A be a determinant-one affine image compressing x_1 by
1/(2d), and B_L the determinant-one image stretching x_1 by L>1.
The compensating inverse scale can be put in a second coordinate.
Both marked bodies have volume V and energy V, independently of L.

Put these bodies at bases -1,1, and use their actual Minkowski midpoint
as the middle fiber. Mark all fibers at zero. The ambient halfspace

    H={x_1+z>=0}

has fixed endpoint mark offsets -1,+1, with mean zero. Its A trace is
empty because max_A x_1=1/2<1. Its B_L trace has the exact volume

    V[(d+1/L)/(d+1)]^d -> Gamma V.                   (3)

The whole construction is an actual compatible convex family. Since
the mark on B is contained in the cap, its ordinary own credit Gamma V
is a universal lower bound, and (3) shows that this is the SHARP
infimum of the endpoint sum using only these fixed endpoint volumes,
energies, and numeric opposite offsets. It gives no improved pair
credit. The target fiber's own geometry is not held fixed here and
may still carry additional information.

## 4. Comparison with the archived obstructions

The d=200 example in
`candidate 2d5ed8c78661db43`
already permits EXACT own-fiber depth at every anchor. Replacing that
quantity by D cannot repair its common-template certificate failure.
Its actual safe cap argument retains unpaired original endpoint
geometry; that information is absent from the scalar replacement.

The exact nonaffine three-interval family in
`candidate 9a6be4fc7a226f55`
already defeats every qualified base-entropy escort. In d=1, D is
exact own depth, so refining the E-to-own-depth conversion has no
slack at all to recover there. These observations do not prohibit
new proofs retaining actual directional section scales or coupled
target/source cap geometry. They close the immediate scalar assembly
and selector substitutions, rather than restating them as conjectures.
